top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) ranks first on the common criteria. Her voice is distinctive, and her formal invention carries feeling. In Autobiography of Red the Stesichorus material becomes a verse novel of desire and difference. In Nox an elegy is made through translating Catullus 101. Her essays from Eros the Bittersweet onward belong to the same practice. The citation should rest on the established core of original poetry, verse narrative, elegy and essay. It should name translation as part of one practice and should not claim that post-2010 work equals the core. That later work is unverified, and the typography and book-design dependence may not survive translation or ordinary editions. These are real reservations. I still judge her case somewhat stronger than that of Cărtărescu (P002), whose single, large imaginative project is serious and distinctive. The difference is one of weighting, concentrated formal renewal against expansive construction, and I cannot test the late Romanian novels directly. Support from four members is not a literary reason. This ranking rests on public knowledge and translations, and I have verified no text independently. P000 ranks last because two serious, single-writer proposals with specific citation scopes are available.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. For context only, my scholarly work on the literary fragment, translation, Paul Celan and exile literature overlaps thematically with parts of Carson's practice. It records no personal, professional or family connection to Carson or Cărtărescu, and it is not evidence of a preference. Chairing the committee and giving ceremony speeches on behalf of the Academy do not establish a personal vote. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
